question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.4$ | $0.1$ |

Given that $\text{E}[X]=2$ and $\text{E}[Y]=1.2,$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2},
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.4$ | $0.1$ | $0.5$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.6$ | $0.4$ | $1$ |

Now, we can find $\text{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a support ${S}_{X},$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{x}^{2}\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & ={1}^{2}\cdot 0.5+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.5 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =5-{2}^{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a support ${S}_{Y},$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}{y}^{2}\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & ={0}^{2}\cdot 0.6+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.4 \\  & =3.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =3.6-{1.2}^{2} \\  & =2.16.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's find $\text{Cov}[X,Y].$ By the rule of the lazy statistician, we find $\text{E}[XY]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}xy\cdot f(x,y) \\  & =(1)(0)f(1,0)+(3)(0)f(3,0)+(1)(3)f(1,3)+(3)(3)f(3,3) \\  & =0\cdot 0.2+0\cdot 0.4+3\cdot 0.3+9\cdot 0.1 \\  & =1.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =1.8-2\cdot 1.2 \\  & =-0.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -0.6 \\ -0.6 & 2.16\end{aligned}].
$$
